art.subject: Ryukyu Flycatcher (Ficedula owstoni), adult male, a spring vagrant in Korean island woodland: crown, nape and back olive-green; a broad yellow supercilium running from the bill to behind the eye; rump yellow; wings blackish with a white patch on the inner greater coverts; tail blackish; throat yellow with an orange tinge, breast yellow, fading to whitish on the lower belly and undertail coverts. Bill short and dark; eye dark; legs dark grey.
art.pose: perched on a mossy branch in the shaded mid-storey, side view
art.scene: evergreen broadleaf forest on a southern Korean island in spring (April–May), dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on a mossy branch in shade: compact flycatcher with a rounded head, greenish-tinged dark olive crown, nape and back, dark olive-green lores, cheeks and ear-coverts, yellow supercilium, yellow throat with only a faint orange tinge, yellow breast, blackish wings and tail, short dark bill

adult male, front three-quarter view perched upright: yellow supercilium above dark olive-green cheeks and ear-coverts, greenish-tinged dark olive crown, yellow throat with only a faint orange tinge, yellow breast fading paler on the belly
art.build: Small, compact flycatcher, smaller than a sparrow, with the shape of Narcissus Flycatcher: rounded head, short neck, upright posture in the shaded mid-storey. Bill short, flat and dark, much shorter than the head. Legs short and dark grey. Tail medium length and square, without white sides.
avoid: Do not paint a black back, crown and tail like male Narcissus Flycatcher; the upperparts are olive-green.
Do not paint a white supercilium (Yellow-rumped Flycatcher).
Do not end the yellow at the eye as in Green-backed Flycatcher; the yellow supercilium continues behind the eye.
Do not add wing bars or white tail sides beyond the single white wing patch.
